blocks.etymology: From Middle English welde, wolde, from Old English *weald, weard, variant form of wād, Proto-West Germanic *waiʀd, from Proto-Germanic *waizdaz. Alternatively reborrowed from or contaminated by Anglo-Norman wold, wolde (compare Old French guaide). Doublet of woad. Dutch wouw is derived from the same basic form with -l-.

senses.definition: A joint formed by heating and pressing pieces of metal together.

blocks.etymology: Alteration of well (“boil, rise”), probably influenced by the past participle, welled. Compare cognate Danish vælde, Swedish välla (“boil, rise → to forge weld”).

senses.definition: To join pieces of metal or plastic by heating them until they melt together.

examples.en: The technician welded the two metal frames together.
examples.vi: Người thợ kỹ thuật đã hàn hai khung kim loại lại với nhau.

senses.vi: hàn

senses.definition: To join people or things closely together to make a strong unit.

examples.en: Shared hardship helped weld the team into a united group.
examples.vi: Gian nan cùng trải qua đã giúp gắn kết cả đội thành một khối thống nhất.

senses.vi: gắn kết; gắn chặt

thesaurus.definition: join together by heating
unite closely or intimately

wiktionary.gloss: To join two materials (especially two metals) together by applying heat, pressure and filler, either separately or in any combination.

examples: I've welded a metal sculpture.
wiktionary.gloss: To make something by welding.

examples: The arrows pierced through the welded ranks of the opposing army.
to weld an alliance
wiktionary.gloss: To bind together inseparably; to unite closely or intimately.

idioms.gloss: To weld using an arc created by electricity.
To position and secure pieces of work using small welded joints at isolated points (typically, in preparation for the final weld).
To join pieces of metal using spot welding
To weld using the stick welding method.

To weld without filler metals, by setting the pieces apart and applying an electric current so that the gap creates resistance and produces the arc required to melt the pieces so they can be pressed together.
